Subject: Spike in April — need reconciliation and proposed path forward

Hi Tessa / Ben,

Hope you’re both well. We just closed our month and noticed a large spike in inference hours for April that pushed us significantly over our committed capacity for Q2. The invoice we received today shows a one-time overage that was higher than expected.

We don’t dispute the usage numbers but we’d like to avoid a prolonged billing fight. Can Redwood propose a fair catch‑up plan that preserves our renewal timeline? Specifically we’re asking:

- A clear breakout of the April spike by service/model (we need CSV export).
- A proposed one‑time settlement amount or amortization over next invoices.
- Whether Redwood can offer any goodwill credit or amnesty for part of the overage given our recent expansion work.

If possible we’d like a single sideletter that documents the one‑time settlement + how future capacity will be adjusted so procurement can sign quickly. We’re aiming to finalize before our renewal on 2026‑06‑01.

Thanks — attaching a short note from our finance team as internal context.

Best,
Anya Patel

Thanks — I reviewed Ben's export. A couple of finance constraints to flag:

- We can approve a one‑time goodwill credit up to 12% of the gross overage for strategic customers; 10% is within that threshold.
- For accounting simplicity I prefer amortization over a fixed number of billing cycles rather than discounting the invoice line item retroactively. Three months is easiest for revenue recognition, but two months is acceptable if the customer signs the sideletter and the AR team issues a clear invoice schedule.
- We need the sideletter to include: (a) exact overage calculation, (b) payment schedule, (c) explicit statement that this is a one‑time settlement and not a precedent for future spikes, (d) approval block for Redwood finance.

I drafted a short sideletter (attached) with placeholders for the dollar amounts and payment dates. If you want to proceed with Ben's recommendation (10% amnesty + two‑month amortization) I’ll finalize the numbers and Rafael (finance) will route approval.

Attachment: sideletter-draft.pdf

Hi Anya / Marco,

Thanks again for flagging this and for the quick call earlier this week. We reviewed the April usage and have a proposal that should keep your renewal on schedule and limit short‑term cash impact. Summary below — full sideletter and invoice attached for signature:

What happened
- A marketing campaign on April 14–15 produced an unexpected burst on the opt‑7b endpoint; the excess above the committed capacity totaled 14,300 inference hours.

Our proposal (recommended)
- Gross overage (before concession): $28,600
- Goodwill concession: 10% amnesty = $2,860
- Net catch‑up owed: $25,740
- Payment plan: two equal installments on the next two invoices (due 2026‑06‑01 and 2026‑07‑01). We will issue an invoice for the first installment on 2026‑05‑18.
- Sideletter: we will provide a one‑time sideletter documenting the calculation and the one‑time nature of this settlement.

Why this path
- Keeps renewal timeline intact (no hold on renewal signature).
- Minimizes one‑time cash pressure for Brightline while keeping revenue recognition straightforward for Redwood.

Next steps
1) Please review the attached sideletter and sign via the DocuSign link below if you accept the terms.
   - Sideletter: sideletter-draft.pdf (attached)
   - DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/BR-2931/sideletter
2) If you’d rather a single one‑time invoice, let us know and we’ll issue it by 2026‑05‑18.
3) Lauren will follow up to confirm the renewal promo remains as discussed and to update the contract baseline if you choose to add committed capacity for Q3.

Attachments: sideletter-draft.pdf; brightline_invoice_202605.pdf; usage_report_may2026.csv

If we don’t hear back by EOD Tuesday (2026‑05‑18) we’ll issue the first installment invoice as outlined.
